problem: Intel had to price memory cheaply against competitors, which hurt overall profits.
title: Intel exits the memory chip business to focus on microprocessors
context: Intel invented DRAM memory and saw itself as the DRAM company, but memory had become a drain on profits.
decision_made: Leave the DRAM business and concentrate on microprocessors.
action_taken: Announced to staff on 10 October 1985 and announced the 80386 microprocessor a week later.
observed_outcome: Grove later called it the best business decision the company ever made. The sources used do not give measured financial results.
lessons: Asking what a new leader would do can free a company from sunk-cost attachment to a core business.
limitations: The positive judgement is the decision-maker's own in retrospect. The anecdote about imagining being fired is from a secondary account. Financial results were not checked.

claims.claim_text: Moore and Grove recommended leaving DRAM in 1985 and Intel announced its withdrawal from the market.
Grove later described the move as the best business decision the company ever made.
